geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

events.title: American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez
events.note: Free screening on the founder of El Teatro Campesino, who built a theatre out of the Delano grape strike and then wrote Zoot Suit. The library programmes this kind of thing better than anyone charges for.

events.title: Unfiltered: What happened to the American Dream?
events.note: Fifteen dollars including dinner, which is the real news. The Club's panel format is reliably better than its titles suggest.

events.title: Soulfly, Nailbomb & Incite
events.note: Max Cavalera playing both of his bands in one night: Soulfly's tribal groove metal and Nailbomb, the industrial side project with Fudge Tunnel's Alex Newport that barely ever tours. The Nailbomb half is the reason to go.

events.title: Free string quartet concert
events.note: Led by the SF Ballet Orchestra's concertmaster, in the Conservatory's recital hall, for nothing. Free chamber music of this standard is rare enough that it belongs near the top of a Monday.

events.title: The Rat Utopia Experiment, False Flag & Fatale
events.note: The club bills the headliner as circus punk, which undersells how grimy it gets; False Flag and Fatale are straight hardcore underneath. One of the last autumns in this room before it closes at the end of the year.

events.title: EsDeeKid with Rico Ace
events.note: Liverpool rapper on the Council House Rat tour — UK drill rewired for a nasal, almost comic delivery that has made him the most argued-about British rapper of the year. A 3,300-seat room is a big swing for a first headline run here.

events.title: Mountain Grass Unit
events.note: Sold out. Alabama bluegrass played by people in their early twenties at a tempo that suggests they have somewhere to be. The basement room is the right size for it.

events.title: She & Him with Jordana
events.note: Sold out. Zooey Deschanel and M. Ward doing Brill Building pastiche with real affection, which the picture palace suits better than a club would.

events.title: Monday Night Hubba: Sea Cruise
events.note: Hubba Hubba Revue's weekly burlesque and variety show in the room above the club, this week a nautical birthday bill for one of its own. Smaller and looser than the troupe's monthly spectaculars. Doors at eight, 18+.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The oldest weekly goth-industrial dance night anywhere, every Monday since 1993: six DJs across two rooms playing gothic, industrial and synthpop. 18+, and five dollars before 10:30, which is hard to beat on any night of the week.

events.title: Toadies with Local H
events.note: Two bands who each had exactly one enormous 1990s single and then spent thirty years being better than it. Toadies' Rubberneck still swings harder than its reputation; Local H are a two-piece who sound like four.

events.title: @ and YHWH Nailgun
events.note: YHWH Nailgun make the most physically disorienting rhythm music of the last two years - drums played like a malfunction, vocals somewhere between yelp and siren. From the ticketing sweep; Cornerstone's own calendar did not list tonight.

events.title: Bobby McFerrin
events.note: Four octaves and no instrument. McFerrin at the Freight is a seated listening-room proposition, not a greatest-hits set, and he improvises most of it on the night. Sourced from the JamBase mirror because thefreight.org blocks automated reads.

events.title: Breadboarding modular synthesizers
events.note: Hands-on workshop building oscillators from loose components rather than buying a module. The practical end of Gray Area's remit and the only thing in the region tonight that sends you home with a circuit.

events.title: Derrick Gee's Radio Hour
events.note: The Australian broadcaster who turned taste-explaining into a genre, doing it live. Gray Area's Grand Theater is the right room for an hour that is half lecture, half listening party.

events.title: Euge Groove
events.note: First of two nights. Smooth jazz played straight by a saxophonist who did his time in Tower of Power's horn section, so the funk underneath is real.

events.title: Jon Guerra & John Mark Comer
events.note: Hushed devotional songwriting paired with a spoken-word segment — closer to a listening service than a gig. Found in the ticketing sweep; the venue did not publish a start time.

events.title: Lee DeWyze with August Lee Stevens
events.note: The ticketing sweep puts this here tonight; the Chapel's own calendar shows nothing on the 5th. One of the two is wrong — check before you go.

events.title: Nick Hakim with Arima Ederra
events.note: Smeared, narcotic soul in the lineage of Shuggie Otis more than of anyone currently working — guitar played like a rumour. August Hall publishes no door times, so confirm before you plan the evening around it.

events.title: Psychotic Reaction & Bongfather
events.note: Garage-punk and stoner riffs in the Mission's smallest serious stage. Lineup detail came from the ticketing sweep only, so treat the billing as provisional.

events.title: The Flatlanders with Jaimee Harris
events.note: Joe Ely, Jimmie Dale Gilmore and Butch Hancock have been the best songwriting trio in Texas since 1972 and tour as a unit perhaps once a decade. That is the whole argument for driving to Novato on a Monday.

events.title: Free first Tuesday at the Legion of Honor
events.note: Same arrangement as the de Young, and the better building of the two — a colonnade above Lands End with Rodin in the courtyard.

events.title: Free first Tuesday at the de Young
events.note: General galleries free to everyone on the first Tuesday of the month — not just Bay Area residents. Special exhibitions still ticket separately.

events.title: Free first Tuesday at the Conservatory of Flowers
events.note: The 1879 glasshouse, free on the first Tuesday. The highland tropics room is the one people come back for, and it is warm, which matters in October fog.

events.title: Pay what you wish at the Cartoon Art Museum
events.note: First Tuesday of the month, name your own admission. A small single-subject museum that takes its subject completely seriously.

events.title: User Experience: interactive tech-art exhibition
events.note: The one piece of SF Tech Week that is open to the public without a badge — a free walk-in exhibition of interactive work off Union Square. The rest of the week is a conference and is not listed here.

events.title: Fleet Week: Navy brass quintet at Salesforce Park
events.note: Military brass in the rooftop park above the transit centre — the first of the week's neighbourhood band concerts, all free and all unannounced until a few days out.

events.title: Made in SF: Dogpatch manufacturing walk
events.note: Free walking tour of the workshops and small factories still operating in Dogpatch, which is a more interesting neighbourhood on foot than its new buildings suggest.

events.title: Muni Bussin' Bingo
events.note: Transit-agency bingo in a Cole Valley taproom, free with RSVP. Exactly the kind of civic oddity this digest exists to find, and the prizes are reportedly Clipper credit.

events.title: Fleet Week: brass band at Noe Valley Town Square
events.note: An hour of service band repertoire in the 24th Street square, free and entirely uncomplicated. Bring a layer; it drops cold the moment the sun clears the hill.

events.title: Arrows In Action with Good Boy Daisy & Instant Crush
events.note: Sold out. Glossy emo-pop with a three-band bill and a 7pm start, so it is over early.

events.title: Jungle with Rio Kosta
events.note: Sold out, and a second night was added for Wednesday. Jungle's modern-disco revue is built for exactly this venue — a hillside amphitheatre at dusk, full choreography, no gaps between songs. The best-matched booking to its room all week.

events.title: Mia Asano & DEADGRACE
events.note: Electric violin run through metal pedals and a backing track — more coherent live than the premise sounds. Eleven dollars is the cheapest ticket in the South Bay this week.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: The Mischief company's catastrophe-comedy, mid-run to late November. Tuesday is the cheapest night and the cast is still finding new ways to break the set.

events.title: The Menzingers with Hot Water Music & Weakened Friends
events.note: Sold out. Scranton's finest hangover-punk songwriters, with Hot Water Music — twenty-eight years of Gainesville melodic hardcore — underneath them. The support act is arguably the bigger deal.

events.title: Free Rugby 101 crash course
events.note: Ninety minutes of being taught to watch the game by people who play it. Venue was not named in the listing, which is the only reason this is marked low.

events.title: Free ballet class with Kathy Mata
events.note: Open adult class, free, no experience assumed — she has run these for decades. The exact studio address was not published with the listing.

events.title: Cavetown with chloe moriondo
events.note: Bedroom pop that grew into a 2,800-cap room without losing the ukulele. The crowd is the event as much as the band is.

events.title: Cure for Paranoia with AroMa
events.note: Dallas collective who play hip-hop as a live band rather than over tracks — closer to a soul revue with rapping than to a rap show.

events.title: Evening Elephants
events.note: Local indie with a jammy streak, playing the back room of a Shattuck beer hall. Low stakes and no cover charge worth arguing about.

events.title: PRESIDENT with Showing Teeth & Cenobia
events.note: The anonymous, masked British hardcore project whose entire identity is withheld information. Whether that survives a 1,400-cap room is the interesting part.

events.title: Sammy Rae & The Friends with Melt
events.note: First of two nights, and the one still on sale. A horn-heavy, deliberately joyful live band whose audience sings every word; Wednesday is already gone.

events.title: Telescreens
events.note: Jangling, Smiths-shaped guitar pop from a band who understand that the chorus is a structural element, not a decoration.

events.title: lilyisthatyou with James the Seventh
events.note: Internet-native pop that is sharper written than its delivery system suggests. An early headline date in a room she will outgrow.

events.title: zzzahara, Faerybabyy & fime
events.note: Co-headline between zzzahara's Los Angeles bedroom pop and Faerybabyy's surf-goth post-punk, with fime's shoegaze opening. The best-sequenced small bill of the midweek.

events.title: Drive-in movie night
events.note: Six dollars a car-seat at one of the last operating drive-ins in Northern California. Concord is a long way from anywhere, and the novelty is the point.

events.title: Benmont Tench
events.note: Forty-seven years as the Heartbreakers' organist, now a solo writer with a voice like a worn hinge. The Freight's seated silence is what these songs need.

events.title: CORPSE DUST with Brood Faye & Edgar SKOTO
events.note: Local noise-punk triple bill found only in the ticketing sweep; nothing about the billing could be confirmed against the venue.

events.title: Dennis Mitcheltree
events.note: Post-bop tenor in the basement jazz room under Annie Street. He plays Oakland's Soundroom on Thursday too, which is the better-sounding of the two options.

events.title: Euge Groove
events.note: Second and final night of the run. Tuesday is the easier room to get into.

events.title: Kelly McFarling with Desiree Cannon
events.note: One of the Bay's steadiest country-folk songwriters in a 150-cap room that nearly went dark last year. Desiree Cannon's harmonies are the reason this bill works.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Night two of a six-night Fillmore residency — the band is playing 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 11 October, rotating the setlist nightly. A residency of that length in a 1,315-cap room is the most generous thing any touring act has done here this year.

events.title: aespa
events.note: Arena K-pop, listed for completeness rather than discovery — if you want this you already have a ticket. BART Coliseum puts you at the door and spares you the $30 lot.

events.title: Fleet Week at Pier 39
events.note: Eleven hours of free Fleet Week programming on the pier — bands, service displays, and the first day the ships are alongside. Drive and you will pay for it; take Muni.

events.title: Free admission day at the SF Zoo
events.note: Free for San Francisco residents with ID. Out at the ocean end of Sloat, so dress for weather that bears no relation to downtown's.

events.title: Free first Wednesday at the GLBT History Museum
events.note: Free on the first Wednesday, in a single Castro storefront that holds the best-kept queer archive on the West Coast. Harvey Milk's kitchen table is in there.

events.title: Free gallery admission at YBCA
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Free every Wednesday, which is the institution's whole point. Three shows up: Dread Scott's The Body Politic, Rael San Fratello's Prototypes and Provocations, and GaHee Park's surrealist paintings.

events.title: Fleet Week: brass quintet at the VA Medical Center
events.note: A service band playing for patients, open to the public. The least publicised and most affecting of the week's free concerts.

events.title: Fleet Week: USAF Band of the Golden West
events.note: The Air Force's regional band on the square. Free, outdoors, and over in an hour.

events.title: Free art workshop: clay vessel sculpture
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two hours of hand-building in the Grand Lobby, free with registration, materials included. Pairs with the free gallery day.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong (matinee)
events.note: The Wednesday matinee, which is the easiest ticket of the week in a run that goes to late November.

events.title: Free bandshell concert
events.note: Three hours at the Music Concourse bandshell for nothing. The Golden Gate Park Band's 144th season closed on 27 September, so this is a one-off rather than the standing Sunday fixture.

events.title: Beyond Walls: human chain around the artwork
events.note: A participatory ring of people around a public sculpture, free with RSVP. Fifteen minutes of your day and the sort of thing you either walk past or join.

events.title: Perfect Blue
events.note: Satoshi Kon's 1997 identity-collapse thriller, which invented a visual grammar that Black Swan later borrowed wholesale. Best seen with strangers.

events.title: Wrathbone
events.note: One-off genre screening in the Roxie's small room. The 16th Street repertory calendar is the densest in the city this week and almost none of it plays twice.

events.title: Films by the COUSIN Collective and Christophe Katrib
events.note: Mill Valley Film Festival programming playing on this side of the bay — experimental shorts from an Indigenous-led collective. BAMPFA is carrying six MVFF slots this week, which saves Berkeley the drive to Marin.

events.title: Free public talk: finding Earth 2.0
events.note: Foothill's astronomy lecture series, free and genuinely technical — exoplanet detection methods rather than wonder-at-the-cosmos filler. The Peninsula's only listing tonight.

events.title: Ilana Glazer Live!
events.note: Post-Broad City stand-up that has got noticeably stranger and more personal. A 7pm start in a 2,800-cap room, so it is out by nine.

events.title: Jungle with Rio Kosta
events.note: Second night, added after the first sold out, and still the better of the two tickets to chase because nobody has it yet.

events.title: Oakland Originals screening with live Q&A
events.note: Five dollars for locally made film with the people who made it in the room, in a 1926 picture palace with a Wurlitzer. The best-value film ticket in the region this week.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Evening performance. Two hours five with an interval, and the set destroys itself on schedule.

events.title: Traveling Shoes
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Sold out. A performance staged inside the Dread Scott exhibition rather than in a theatre, which changes what the work is doing. Free, but gone.

events.title: Dracula (preview)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: First of three previews before Saturday's opening. Steven Dietz's adaptation, directed by TheatreWorks' Giovanna Sardelli — the Dietz version keeps Stoker's epistolary structure, which is why it stays creepy rather than camp.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Opening night of a twelve-day run of Cameron Mackintosh's restaged tour — Bjornson's original designs, Prince's blocking, a smaller pit. The chandelier still does the thing.

events.title: sombr with Tom Odell & The Hellp
events.note: An arena show for an artist whose songs are mostly whispered, which will either be moving or inaudible. Tom Odell in support is the stronger live proposition.

events.title: Anna Graves with Emma Roellig
events.note: Close-miked songwriting in the basement, the kind of bill where the room goes quiet without being asked.

events.title: Ariel Elias
events.note: Standing weekly programming at the South Bay's long-running comedy club; listed for completeness. Elias is the one who drank a heckler's beer on camera and is better than that clip.

events.title: Deer Tick with Presley Haile
events.note: Providence's shambolic Americana lifers, who are far tighter than their reputation and funnier than almost anyone touring.

events.title: Filipinana
events.note: Part of the FiliKula series — a slow, funny study of class seen from a golf course's caddy shack. Second of two screenings this week.

events.title: Jacob Alon with dogpatch
events.note: Fife-born songwriter whose debut arrived fully formed — queer Celtic folk sung in a high, unguarded voice. The wooden upstairs hall is the right building for it.

events.title: Lloyd Cole (solo electric)
events.note: Sold out. Forty years of the most literate guitar pop Britain produced, played alone with an electric and a dry wit. Rattlesnakes still scans.

events.title: Rocky Dale Davis
events.note: Chain-club booking, listed for completeness. Alabama storytelling, slow delivery, more craft than the podcast circuit implies.

events.title: Sammy Rae & The Friends with Melt
events.note: Sold out — second of two nights. If you want in, Tuesday is the one with tickets.

events.title: Son Lux with MMEADOWS
events.note: Moved here from the UC Theatre, which means a 300-cap room for a band who scored Everything Everywhere All At Once. Ryan Lott writes for the gaps between instruments; the smaller room helps.

events.title: Stephen Dawes with Jojomber
events.note: Warm, unhurried guitar pop with a Laurel Canyon hangover. Rickshaw remains the best-value 400-cap room in the city.

events.title: The Dresden Dolls with OBSIDIENNE OBSURD
events.note: Amanda Palmer and Brian Viglione's cabaret-punk duo, intact, in a gilded room with a balcony — which is where this music was always headed. Theatre, not nostalgia.

events.title: The Spiral Electric, Fake Your Own Death & Silent Pictures
events.note: Three local bands working the same neo-psych and post-punk seam from different ends. Fifteen dollars for a full night.

events.title: Dead Souls
events.note: Late-night programming at the Roxie, the only cinema in town that still treats 8:30pm as early.

events.title: The Animeros with Edgar
events.note: Cumbia and surf guitar welded together with enough reverb to flood the room. A late start even for a Wednesday.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T.'s staging of the Hitchcock, mid-run to 18 October — four actors, a lot of projection, the crop-duster done live. A.C.T. publishes no per-date curtain times on its listings page, so confirm the time when you book.

events.title: Artificial Muscle with Welcome StrawberrySparkler
events.note: Oakland noise-rock in the smallest room on this list. Sourced via JamBase because the club's own calendar renders client-side and fetches empty.

events.title: Fleet Week ship tours
events.note: Free public tours of the visiting warships, first-come and screened at the gate, running through 12 October. Today and tomorrow are the quiet days — once the Blue Angels arrive the queue doubles.

events.title: French Police
events.note: Chicago post-punk sung mostly in Spanish, built on one chorused guitar tone and total commitment to it. No door time published.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Night three of six. Midweek nights in a residency are where the deep cuts live.

events.title: The Neighbourhood with AfterNoise Dept
events.note: Reunited after a five-year hiatus, playing the monochrome moodiness that defined a particular 2013. A 7,000-cap barn is a lot of room for it.

events.title: Kidquake: upper elementary
events.note: Free, in the Main Library's Koret auditorium: Dan Santat, Elisa Kleven and Lisa Moore Ramee reading to a room of children who have been bussed in. Open to the public too, and nobody tells you that.

events.title: Fleet Week: Navy woodwind quintet at the Ferry Building
events.note: Chamber repertoire under the Ferry Building nave at lunchtime, free. The acoustics in there are better than anyone intends.

events.title: Lunchtime concert: Quinteto Latino
events.note: A Latin American wind quintet on the Great Lawn, free, at lunchtime. Quinteto Latino commission new work rather than recycling the canon, which is why they are worth sitting down for.

events.title: Blue Angels arrival and practice flights
events.note: The practice day, and the local secret: same aircraft, same bay, a fraction of the crowd. Four hours of survey passes between the bridge and Alcatraz with room to sit down.

events.title: Fleet Week: USAF Band brass at Fisherman's Wharf
events.note: Free brass on the Wharf, which is where Fleet Week's centre of gravity sits all week.

events.title: The Cook (matinee)
events.note: Closed-captioned, with a post-show discussion. Eduardo Machado's forty-year vigil in a Havana mansion, in the Peet's Theatre, closing Sunday.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Thursday matinee, and the cheapest seats of the run. Closed-captioned performance.

events.title: Fleet Week Heroes Block Party
events.note: Two blocks of North Beach closed off for a free street party, food and drink for sale. The Fleet Week event most likely to be full of people who are not there for Fleet Week.

events.title: Fleet Week: Navy brass band in the Castro
events.note: A service band playing the Castro at rush hour, in the plaza at Castro and Market. The juxtaposition is the event.

events.title: Fleet Week: USAF Band of the Golden West (Mobility)
events.note: The Air Force band's pop-covers unit, which is more fun than the brass ensembles and knows it. Free on the pier.

events.title: Valencia Live night market
events.note: The last Valencia Live of 2026 — the street closed to cars from 18th to 21st, vendors, food and sound systems for five hours. Free, and the car-free Valencia experiment's best argument for itself. BART 16th St, five minutes.

events.title: Honor Our Fallen concert
events.note: Free with a reservation, and the one Fleet Week event that is not a spectacle — a ceremonial band concert in a 650-seat theatre built as a memorial. Reserve ahead; it is not a walk-up.

events.title: KPFA presents: The People's History
events.note: Free with registration. KPFA has been doing this since 1949 and the live events are better than the pledge drives suggest.

events.title: NightLife
events.note: The standing Thursday adults-only museum night, 21+, with DJs and a bar among the exhibits. The Academy's page did not state this week's theme, so the programming is unconfirmed even though the night itself runs weekly.

events.title: SF Election 2026: big donors and power grabs
events.note: Free with RSVP in the Richmond's former Christian Science church, which is the best room for a public argument in this city. Local-politics reporting rather than campaigning.

events.title: Thursday night poem jam
events.note: Open-mic poetry in a public library, free, no sign-up fee and no drink minimum. The antithesis of the paid reading series.

events.title: Unzipped
events.note: Douglas Keeve's 1995 Isaac Mizrahi documentary, which invented the modern fashion film and is funnier than anything that followed it.

events.title: Workshop: writing hard enough to shift gravity
events.note: Free generative writing workshop in the Main Library, during Litquake week, which is either a coincidence or good planning.

events.title: Dying Fetus with Sanguisugabogg, Crowbar, Left to Suffer & Deterioration
events.note: Five bands, a 6:30 start, and Crowbar — thirty-six years of New Orleans sludge — buried third on the bill, which is the real value here. Arrive early or you will miss the best set.

events.title: Fleet Week: Navy Band Southwest Destroyers
events.note: The Navy's rock band playing the Chinese-American veterans' post in Chinatown. Free, indoors, and the smallest room any of these bands play this week.

events.title: Free talk: Ocean Beach and the Fort Funston dunes
events.note: The native plant society on the only dune ecosystem left in the city. Free, donations welcome, and the slides are usually extraordinary.

events.title: King Lear
events.note: Final week of a Mission staging that closes Sunday. Z Space's shows are linked individually off its homepage rather than from a calendar, which is why this production goes unreported most weeks.

events.title: Litquake opening night: the Booksellers Ball
events.note: Litquake's 27th festival opens here — an open bar, a BFF.FM DJ, and a literature-themed drag turn from Carlota Di Carlo, with the money going to put booksellers and librarians in the room. Seventeen days of readings follow, to 24 October.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Thursday evening; a $5-off code was circulating for tonight's performance.

events.title: SpookFest 2026
events.note: The Roxie's horror programme kicking off for October. Expect prints in varying states of health, which is part of the deal.

events.title: Union Town
events.note: Mill Valley Film Festival at BAMPFA. Labour documentary; the festival's Berkeley slots are the cheapest way into MVFF without crossing a bridge.

events.title: Dracula (preview)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Second preview. Preview pricing holds until Saturday's opening, which makes tonight the value proposition.

events.title: JO1
events.note: Japanese boy group formed on a Korean-format survival show, touring North America on the ANIMAL record. Choreography-first, and the Warfield floor will be entirely lightsticks.

events.title: Mumford & Sons with Sierra Ferrell
events.note: The biggest ticket of the week and the closest to this digest's starting point — two miles. Sierra Ferrell is the reason to arrive on time: Appalachian singing with a jazz singer's phrasing, and she will be headlining places this size herself soon.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Second of two performances today. Two and a half hours including the interval.

events.title: Zoe Presents: Memorex + Rexsexex y Mas
events.note: A curated programme of video-art oddities. The Roxie gives its 8pm slot to things like this and no other cinema here does.

events.title: Autumn Bruewer
events.note: Standing weekly programming at the Sunnyvale club; listed for completeness.

events.title: Evangelia with STOLAR & Aristea Taptelis
events.note: Greek-American pop that folds rebetiko melody into club production without treating it as costume. Three acts, 8pm start.

events.title: LOLO with Mylie Taylor
events.note: Canadian pop-punk with the hooks placed where they do the most damage. A small room for an act with this much streaming traction.

events.title: La Mole
events.note: Spanish-language stand-up at the chain club, listed for completeness. Spanish-language comedy tours the South Bay more than any English-language act and gets written about less.

events.title: Mon Rovia with Sydney Rose & Sarah Julia
events.note: Sold out. Liberian-born, Tennessee-raised songwriter whose Afro-Appalachian framing is not a marketing line — banjo tuned against West African melody, sung very quietly.

events.title: The Breaks
events.note: A live band playing breakbeats as repertoire — the records samplers raided, performed whole. More interesting than a DJ set and sweatier than a revue.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Evening performance in the final week. A cook keeps a promise to an owner who never comes back, and Cuba changes around her — the best-constructed script in the region right now.

events.title: The Living Tombstone
events.note: Fan-music turned touring act — the Israeli-American project that built an audience entirely out of video-game songs and now fills a 3,000-cap hall with it. Genuinely odd and genuinely popular.

events.title: Thinking Fellers Union Local 282 with Bill Orcutt & Famous Mammals
events.note: A San Francisco institution almost nobody outside this city has heard of — forty years of deliberately broken song structures — with Bill Orcutt's solo guitar demolitions opening. The strangest well-made bill of the week.

events.title: Y La Bamba with Vanessa Zamora
events.note: Luz Elena Mendoza Ramos writes in two languages about one border, and the band has got heavier and stranger with every record. The best Latin-adjacent booking in a club this week.

events.title: Casa Sueno, Ray Yeh & Rituals of Mine
events.note: Rituals of Mine closing with Terra Lopez's electronic R&B is the draw; the two local openers are post-punk and indie-pop respectively. The ticketing sweep lists a completely different bill for tonight — the club's own calendar is the one to trust.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T., mid-run. Curtain time is not published per date on the theatre's listings page - confirm when booking.

events.title: Amarok with Demonsmoke & In Shame
events.note: Doom in the back of a pizza place, which is where a lot of Oakland's heavy music actually happens. Billing from the ticketing sweep only.

events.title: Chinese Football
events.note: Wuhan's answer to American Football, complete with the house on the album cover — emo revival played with more precision than its models managed. From the ticketing sweep.

events.title: DJ Leydis
events.note: One of the first women to DJ in Havana, now a fixture here. A rooftop in October is a gamble but she is worth the layers.

events.title: DJ Rabeat with Femmelectric
events.note: Latin club music at Berkeley's fifty-year-old solidarity cultural centre, which remains one of the few places where the politics and the dancing are the same project.

events.title: Dennis Mitcheltree
events.note: The better-sounding of his two Bay dates this week — the Soundroom is a listening room with no bar chatter, which post-bop tenor needs.

events.title: Drag Talk with Filth Is Eternal & Integra Pink
events.note: Hardcore band and drag performers on the same bill, which in this city is less a crossover than a default. Filth Is Eternal are genuinely abrasive.

events.title: Nino Msk & Sonamo
events.note: Divisadero's art bar, which books something most nights and documents almost none of it. Billing unverified.

events.title: Parrotfish with Indigo Elephant
events.note: An all-ages rock bill at a club better known for its dance nights. The date is on DNA's own calendar; nothing more about either band could be confirmed.

events.title: Rachel Bochner
events.note: An artist-run space in the Lower Haight hosting a touring pop songwriter. Capacity is about a living room's worth.

events.title: Rickie Lee Jones
events.note: Clears the drive on legacy alone: Chuck E's in Love is forty-seven years old and she has spent every year since refusing to play it the same way. She also appears at the Freight's gala tomorrow, but that is a fundraiser, not a set.

events.title: Shroud & Young Lovers
events.note: A 150-cap Mission bar with a stage in the corner. Kilowatt's site renders its calendar client-side and fetches empty, so this is the only listing recovered.

events.title: Tahum
events.note: A church-hall booking found only in the ticketing sweep; nothing about the act could be verified. Churches make the best rooms in the city and the worst-documented calendars.

events.title: The Rasmus with Saint Agnes
events.note: Finland's biggest rock export still touring In the Shadows, with London's Saint Agnes doing filthy blues-punk underneath. The support is the better band now.

events.title: Will Downing
events.note: First of two nights. Four decades of what the billing calls sophisticated soul and what is really a jazz singer's approach to R&B ballads. Expensive, and the room is small enough to justify it.

events.title: Xiu Xiu perform Eraserhead
events.note: Jamie Stewart's group scoring Lynch's first feature live. Xiu Xiu have been doing soundtrack commissions for years and this is the pairing that makes most sense: both works are about industrial noise as emotional weather.

events.title: somesurprises with Ilyas Ahmed & Chuck Johnson
events.note: Chuck Johnson's pedal-steel drone work is some of the most beautiful music being made in the Bay Area, and he is opening. Three acts of quiet, patient playing in a 150-cap room.

events.title: SPAM New Media Festival
events.note: Free, all day, and the kind of programme — computer music, performance, installation - that the brief's experimental emphasis has almost nowhere else to look. Indexical is a small Santa Cruz venue punching far above its size.

events.title: Kidquake: lower elementary
events.note: Free: Monisha Bajaj, Maggie Tokuda-Hall and Mahogany L. Browne reading in the Main Library. Browne is a formidable live reader whichever age she is reading to.

events.title: Parade of Ships under the Golden Gate
events.note: The largest parade of ships on the West Coast, led in by a Fire Department fireboat throwing water. One hour, free, and it happens an hour before the air show — Crissy Field gets you both without moving.

events.title: Blue Angels air show, day one
events.note: Four hours over the bay between the Golden Gate and Alcatraz, with the F-22 Raptor and F-35B demo teams either side of the Blue Angels. Free from anywhere on the northern waterfront — Crissy Field, Fort Mason, Aquatic Park, the Marina. Fog is the only thing that cancels it.

events.title: Fleet Week: Navy brass band at the bandshell
events.note: Free at the Music Concourse bandshell, and far enough from the waterfront to be audible over the jets.

events.title: Fleet Week: brass band at Patricia's Green
events.note: Hayes Valley's pocket park gets a service band at lunchtime. Free, twenty minutes' walk from the Civic Center stations.

events.title: Fleet Week: woodwind quintet at the Tunnel Tops
events.note: The best-sited of today's free concerts: a quintet on the Tunnel Tops lawn with the air show happening directly in front of you. Arrive early; this is not a secret.

events.title: 626 Night Market
events.note: Eight dollars for 200-plus food, craft and game stalls modelled on Taiwanese night markets — the biggest of its kind on the West Coast, running all three nights. Pleasanton is in no region list in the brief, so this is filed East Bay by county; it is a real haul from anywhere on this list.

events.title: Slow-paced Golden Gate Park ride
events.note: Free with RSVP, deliberately unhurried, starting at the bandshell. The park's car-free stretches make this a genuinely pleasant two hours rather than a workout.

events.title: When a Witness Recants
events.note: Mill Valley Film Festival at BAMPFA, mid-afternoon. A matinee documentary slot, which is the easiest MVFF ticket to get.

events.title: Fleet Week: popular music group at Union Square
events.note: The covers band rather than the brass ensemble, in the square, free. Better than it needs to be.

events.title: Fleet Week: woodwind quintet at Glen Park Library
events.note: A branch library concert, free, for the people who do not want to be anywhere near the waterfront today. Entirely reasonable position.

events.title: Fridays on Front: Fleet Week yacht rock block party
events.note: Six hours of a closed street in the Financial District with a yacht rock band and open containers, free to enter. The entertainment-zone experiment at its most literal.

events.title: Chinatown Night Market
events.note: Five blocks of Grant closed to cars for dim sum, BBQ skewers, boba, lion dancing and wine gardens — free, and voted the best night market in the country two years running. Second Friday of the month, May to October, so this is the penultimate one of the year. BART Montgomery or the 30 bus; parking is hopeless.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA with CHIKA DI
events.note: Free, outdoors on the Garden Stage: CHIKA DI's bilingual Afro-Latin and cumbia-pop set, with the galleries open and the food trucks in. The series runs Fridays to the end of October and then stops for the winter, so there are three of these left. BART Lake Merritt is two minutes away and you should use it.

events.title: Ethan Iverson plays James P. Johnson & John Coltrane
events.note: The former Bad Plus pianist drawing a line from Harlem stride to A Love Supreme in a piano showroom, on a very good instrument, for thirty dollars. An early start and the most interesting jazz programme in the region this week.

events.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
events.note: Japanese programming in the Roxie's small room, part of a dense weekend that also carries two festivals.

events.title: Humans Only music showcase in the park
events.note: Free, outdoors, an hour long, and explicitly billed as music made without generative AI - a position that is going to date either very well or very badly.

events.title: Movies at Mechanics'
events.note: The 1854 library's screening room, which has a chess room next door and the best reading chairs in the city. Membership is not required for the film series.

events.title: San Jose State vs Wyoming
events.note: Fifteen dollars for Mountain West football on a Friday night, which is the cheapest live sport in the region and much better atmosphere than the attendance figures imply.

events.title: Second Friday art walk
events.note: Free, and the quieter of Oakland's two monthly art walks — working studios in a warehouse district rather than a closed street. Fruitvale BART then a fifteen-minute walk, or drive and park easily, which is the one place in Oakland that is true.

events.title: New People: NAZA
events.note: From the New People series of contemporary Japanese cinema. Six screenings today across two Roxie screens, which is the busiest the 16th Street calendar gets.

events.title: Apricot Court, A French Project, Total Joke & Something Wicked
events.note: Five dollars, four bands, all ages, volunteer-run, no alcohol, and the same room since 1986. Gilman's calendar sits behind a ticketing link that is usually unreadable — this is the first week in a while it could be reached, so take advantage.

events.title: Elephants in the Fog
events.note: MVFF's Friday evening slot in Berkeley. Two films here today, five more across the weekend.

events.title: Floating Features: Top Gun
events.note: Top Gun on the same day the Blue Angels fly over the bay, which is either lazy or perfect. The Roxie knows exactly what it is doing.

events.title: King Lear
events.note: Penultimate weekend performances of a staging that closes Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Litquake: Hernan Diaz in conversation with Ed Yong
events.note: The Pulitzer-winning novelist of Trust with the Pulitzer-winning science writer of An Immense World, which is a genuinely unexpected pairing and the best Litquake ticket of the opening weekend. Fort Mason, so parking is actually possible.

events.title: Mastodon with Deafheaven & Alcest
events.note: The best-sequenced heavy bill of the year: Alcest invented blackgaze in Bagnols-sur-Ceze, Deafheaven made it American and divisive, and Mastodon turned prog-sludge into stadium music. Three bands who each solved the same problem differently, in a 2,800-cap art deco room. Take BART — downtown Oakland garages shut their gates at seven.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Tucson Roadrunners
events.note: AHL hockey in the small rink next to SAP Center — sixteen dollars, fast, and close enough to hear the bench. Exactly what the brief means by minor-league and atmospheric.

events.title: Traitrs
events.note: Toronto darkwave with the drum machine turned up and the reverb left on everything. The South Bay's only goth-adjacent booking this week.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: Avie Luthra
events.note: The 3rd i South Asian film festival's Roxie slot, with the director present. 3rd i has run here for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Mortified
events.note: Adults reading their own teenage diaries, poems and letters aloud to strangers — every second Friday, and funnier than the premise because nobody wrote the material to be funny. All ages, doors 6:30; general admission does not guarantee a seat.

events.title: Cam Bertrand
events.note: Two shows tonight, 7:30 and 9:45. Standing club programming, listed for completeness.

events.title: Dracula (final preview)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Last preview before Saturday's opening, and the final night at preview prices.

events.title: Rumours of Fleetwood Mac
events.note: A tribute act, listed because the hillside above Saratoga is a genuinely lovely place to be at dusk and the band play the Rumours material straight. The shuttle from the lower lot is not optional.

events.title: Smuin: French Kiss
events.note: Opening night, with a meet-and-greet. Smuin opens its 26/27 season with a triple bill: Amy Seiwert's French Kiss, Michael Smuin's Stabat Mater revived, and a world premiere by My'Kal Stromile. The Cowell Theater is in the same Fort Mason building whose public calendar lists only the galleries, which is why a full SF dance run went unlisted here until now.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Friday pricing is the steepest of the run. The Thursday matinee is half this.

events.title: Bit Brigade with Slowly Crushed
events.note: A band that plays a video game's entire soundtrack live while a fifth member speedruns the game on a screen behind them. Absurd, technically astonishing, and completely unreproducible on record.

events.title: DOMi & JD BECK
events.note: Sold out. A keyboard player and a drummer in their twenties playing jazz at hip-hop tempos with cartoon timing. If you missed this, they play the Catalyst in Santa Cruz tomorrow and tickets are thirty-four dollars.

events.title: High on Fire with Windhand & Penury
events.note: Matt Pike's band at their local-ish room, with Windhand's Virginia doom underneath. They play Santa Cruz tomorrow with the Melvins, which is the better bill but a longer drive.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Friday's 8pm curtain, the latest of the week.

events.title: Phillip Phillips with Elias Hix
events.note: The Idol winner who quietly became a competent roots-rock songwriter and has been touring clubs on it ever since. The gilded room flatters him.

events.title: Pink Talking Fish
events.note: Pink Floyd, Talking Heads and Phish material played as one continuous set, which sounds like a bad idea and works more often than it should. Caltrain Menlo Park is four minutes away.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Closing weekend. The Peet's Theatre is the smaller of Berkeley Rep's two houses and the right size for a play that happens almost entirely in one kitchen.

events.title: The Price Is Right Live
events.note: The game show, staged, with audience members actually playing for prizes. Filed under oddities without apology — twenty-eight dollars to spin the wheel is a defensible evening.

events.title: Yung Fazo, Cthrurio, SophomoreNoir & Jsprings
events.note: Four acts from the rage and plugg end of internet rap, which is loud, short and built entirely out of distorted 808s. A young room.

events.title: New People: Never After Dark
events.note: Second New People slot of the evening.

events.title: Chronovisor
events.note: Repeat of Monday's screening for anyone who missed it. Late, and the Roxie's late shows draw the better crowd.

events.title: Cobweb Cabaret
events.note: A Halloween-season variety night — burlesque, aerial, sideshow — in a former mortuary chapel, which is doing a lot of the work. Late start, 9pm.

events.title: Devon Gilfillian with Snacktime
events.note: Nashville soul with a real band behind it, and Philadelphia's Snacktime — a street brass crew who became a touring act — opening. Nine o'clock start, so the night goes long.

events.title: Michigander
events.note: Jason Singer's heartland indie-rock, which is more carefully written than the genre usually allows. Nine o'clock start in the back room.

events.title: Tim Atlas with Mejiwahn & Cheflee
events.note: Smooth, jazz-inflected bedroom R&B from a Bay Area native, with Mejiwahn's woozy folk underneath. Three acts for twenty dollars.

events.title: Club Antonio
events.note: Two floors of house, techno and Latin club music, 21+. The reason to go is Sinkitty — Bogotá-born, New York-based, rebuilding early-2000s reggaeton into something darker and queerer — in what is billed as a San Francisco debut.

events.title: Last Friday Night: Y2K-2010s Throwbacks
events.note: A pop-nostalgia dance night working the decade from Britney to Avicii, one DJ, 18+. Exactly what it says and nothing more; it takes over the main room once Mortified has cleared it.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T. Curtain time unpublished per date; confirm when booking.

events.title: Audien with TELYKAST, Ryos & Amel
events.note: Mainstage progressive house in the Dogpatch warehouse. The Midway is the one large club in the city with easy parking, which is most of why it works.

events.title: BEAT: Belew, Vai, Levin & Bozzio
events.note: Clears the drive easily: Adrian Belew and Tony Levin playing King Crimson's 1980s material with Steve Vai in Fripp's chair and Terry Bozzio behind them. A limestone quarry on the UCSC campus is an absurd and excellent place to hear Discipline played properly.

events.title: Baauer
events.note: A decade past Harlem Shake, Baauer makes genuinely strange bass music that deserves better than the meme. SoMa's best-sounding small club.

events.title: Celebrate the Freight gala with Rickie Lee Jones, Wu Fei & Abigail Washburn
events.note: A fundraiser, so expect speeches, but the bill is real: Rickie Lee Jones, plus Wu Fei's guzheng against Abigail Washburn's clawhammer banjo, which is one of the few genuine East-West collaborations in folk music rather than a gesture at one.

events.title: Dead Kennedys with Flipper & Avengers
events.note: Three bands from the 1977-81 San Francisco punk scene on one bill, in the city that made them, which has not happened in years. Flipper invented a tempo nobody else wanted and the Avengers' Penelope Houston remains the best singer any of these bands had. Biafra is not in the Kennedys and has not been since 1986 — go knowing that, and it is still the most historically loaded ticket of the week.

events.title: El Pecado de Juana with Mala Grena & La Femme Papi
events.note: Spanish-language punk and cumbia in Oakland's smallest serious room. The kind of bill that exists nowhere in the aggregators and is the reason this venue being readable again matters.

events.title: Erasure-Esque with Just Like Heaven & KROME ADDIKT
events.note: Three tribute acts in a 150-cap Albany bar — Erasure, the Cure and Depeche Mode respectively. Listed because the free-and-cheap circuit runs on nights like this, never because it is the best thing on.

events.title: Holy Priest
events.note: Listed on the JamBase mirror for tonight and nowhere else, which is unusual for a room this size. Verify before making plans.

events.title: Monster's Ball
events.note: The Ruckus Revival and Disco Donutz Circus throwing a costume party across both Public Works rooms. Public Works publishes no set times, which is traditional.

events.title: Musiq Soulchild
events.note: First of an eight-night run to 16 October. Philadelphia neo-soul of the Just Friends vintage, in a 400-cap jazz club — a residency of this length by an artist of this size is unusual and the midweek dates will be the loose ones.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Night four of six, and the first weekend night of the residency — expect the longer set and the bigger jams.

events.title: Riordan
events.note: House and UK garage across the multiple floors of 1015. No set times published.

events.title: Roam x Sirens: Man Power, 25 years of Roam
events.note: A quarter-century of one of the city's longest-running house parties, with Man Power headlining. The upstairs room while the Monster's Ball runs below.

events.title: Rod Wave with Fridayy
events.note: Arena rap, listed for completeness. Deprioritised in this digest's brief on the grounds that nobody needs help finding it.

events.title: Slightly Stoopid with The Elovaters, The Hip Abduction & DENM
events.note: Stanford's restored bowl, which is the best outdoor room on the Peninsula and barely used. Stanford is not in any region list in the brief, so this is filed as Peninsula by proximity to Palo Alto.

events.title: Steel Pulse
events.note: Handsworth Revolution is forty-eight years old and David Hinds is still fronting the band that made it — the only British roots-reggae group of that generation still touring with its founder. The one Bay-adjacent date.

events.title: Unseen Visions: a new age music and culture symposium
events.note: A day of films, lectures and performances taking new age music seriously as a Californian art form rather than a joke. Exactly the sort of thing Gray Area exists for.

events.title: Watsky
events.note: A San Francisco rapper who started in slam poetry, playing the restored Presidio theatre - a seated room, which suits a performer whose selling point is words per minute.

events.title: Yellowjackets with Kurt Elling
events.note: Forty-five years of the Yellowjackets' fusion with Kurt Elling's baritone on top, which is a better fit than either party's catalogue suggests. sfjazz.org blocks automated reads, so this came off the JamBase mirror — assume SFJAZZ has more on than this.

events.title: Zacarias Ferreira
events.note: Dominican bachata sung in the high, aching register the genre was built on. Rooms like this one carry most of the region's Spanish-language touring and reach no aggregator.

events.title: Fleet Fest
events.note: Free, eight hours, across Fisherman's Wharf, the SkyStar Wheel and Pier 27: local musicians, military bands, a STEM centre and a readiness expo. The ground-level half of Fleet Week, and the half with the food.

events.title: Free Saturday at the Legion of Honor
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents. The walk out to Lands End afterwards is the real programme.

events.title: Free Saturday at the de Young
events.note: Free for Bay Area residents with ID — a different mechanism from Tuesday's free day, which is open to everyone. Bring proof of address.

events.title: 34th Indigenous Peoples Day Powwow & Indian Market
events.venue: Martin Luther King Jr. Civic Center Park
events.note: Free, eight hours, thirty-fourth year: Berkeley passed the first Indigenous Peoples Day resolution in the United States in 1992 and this powwow is the direct descendant of that vote. Intertribal dancing, drum groups, a full craft and food market, and no admission charge. Downtown Berkeley BART is two blocks away. Nothing else this weekend is both free and this singular.

events.title: Acorn Adventure: intro to needle felting
events.note: Ninety minutes of wool and barbed needles on a working farm in the Los Altos hills. Seventy-five dollars is steep; the setting is the compensation.

events.title: Free outdoor painting gathering
events.note: Bring your own materials and paint the rotunda with other people doing the same. Free, two hours, and directly under the air show's flight path, which will either help or ruin the concentration.

events.title: K9 Heroes
events.note: Free: military and police working-dog demonstrations in the city's most dog-dense park, which is either perfect programming or an act of provocation. Four hours, and the handlers will talk to anyone.

events.title: Paramount Theatre public tour
events.note: Ten dollars to walk through the finest art deco interior on the West Coast with someone who knows what every surface is made of. Two hours, first and third Saturdays, and the only way to see the building when it is not dark.

events.title: TechFest: Cars, Computers on Wheels
events.note: Five hours of hands-on programming about what is actually inside a modern car, in the one museum anywhere that treats computing as history rather than product. Good with children and better than it sounds without them.

events.title: ArtSpan Open Studios pop-up gallery
events.note: A free group show of work by artists on this year's Open Studios roster, in the Bryant Street store. ArtSpan's own weekend-by-weekend neighbourhood schedule could not be confirmed, so the studio tours themselves are not listed here.

events.title: Second Saturdays 'Round the World: Bollywood Garba
events.note: Free garba instruction and dancing in Union Square at the tail of Navratri — three hours, no experience needed, and the teachers are patient. The best free dance event of the week.

events.title: Woodside Day of the Horse: free horse fair
events.note: Free: a horse fair in the middle of Woodside, with breed demonstrations, vaquero tack and the town's entire equestrian apparatus on display. Trail rides are $40-130 and separate. Genuinely unlike anything else on the Peninsula.

events.title: Blue Angels air show, day two
events.note: The main day, and the week's defining event: four hours over the bay between the Golden Gate and Alcatraz, free from any point on the northern waterfront, with the F-22 and F-35B demo teams either side of the Blue Angels. Crissy Field, Fort Mason, Aquatic Park and the Tunnel Tops all work; Marina Green is loudest. Do not drive into the Marina.

events.title: Live on Larkin street festival
events.note: Free: the Tenderloin's own street festival, Little Saigon end of Larkin closed to cars, with Vietnamese food, stages and neighbourhood organisations. Smaller and more local than the big fairs, which is the appeal.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: Sand City
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Oakland Rising: Follow the Music
events.note: Free on the Great Lawn: three hours of East Bay artists brought across the bridge for the Yerba Buena Gardens Festival, which programmes all summer and autumn for nothing and gets almost no coverage.

events.title: Sad Girlz
events.note: MVFF at BAMPFA, first of three today. An early-afternoon slot, which is the civilised way to do a festival.

events.title: San Jose Sharks vs Edmonton Oilers
events.note: A one o'clock NHL start, which is unusual and makes a day of it. Above this digest's minor-league preference, so listed rather than recommended — the Barracuda game at Tech CU tonight is a quarter of the price.

events.title: New People: NAZA
events.note: From the New People strand of contemporary Japanese cinema — a Japantown-rooted series that rarely screens anywhere else in the region. First of two showings today.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong (matinee)
events.note: Saturday matinee, the most family-viable performance of the week.

events.title: The Cook (matinee)
events.note: Audio-described, with a post-show discussion. Penultimate performance.

events.title: The Music Room
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Satyajit Ray's 1958 study of an aristocrat ruining himself for one more concert, screened in YBCA's own room with gallery admission and snacks included in the fifteen dollars. The best-value film ticket in the city today.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Saturday matinee, and the most expensive seat of the entire run. Sunday afternoon is cheaper for the same show.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: TechnoCats
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Traces of Home
events.note: Repeat of the screening that opened the Roxie's week on Monday, for anyone who missed it.

events.title: Minotaur
events.note: Second MVFF slot of the afternoon at BAMPFA.

events.title: Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour (reception)
events.note: Free opening reception on College Avenue for a show running to 14 November. Rockridge's galleries do not get an art walk, so the receptions are the only time the street feels like one.

events.title: New People: NAZA
events.note: From the New People strand of contemporary Japanese cinema — a Japantown-rooted series that rarely screens anywhere else in the region. Second showing.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: The Great Shamsuddin Family
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Filipiñana
events.note: Third screening this week of the FiliKula series' centrepiece — a slow, funny study of class seen from a golf course's caddy shack. Clashes exactly with the 3rd i slot in the other room.

events.title: Cam Bertrand
events.note: Standing club programming, listed for completeness.

events.title: New People: Never After Dark
events.note: From the New People strand of contemporary Japanese cinema — a Japantown-rooted series that rarely screens anywhere else in the region.

events.title: San Jose Barracuda vs Tucson Roadrunners
events.note: Second of a two-game set. Twenty dollars, and you can hear the coaches.

events.title: Bruno Mars with Raye & DJ Pee.Wee
events.note: First of two stadium nights. Listed for completeness and deprioritised on principle — a two-hundred-dollar floor price and 68,000 people is the opposite of what this digest is for. Raye, opening, is the better show.

events.title: King Lear
events.note: Last evening performance; it closes with tomorrow's matinee.

events.title: On Behalf of My Son
events.note: MVFF's Saturday evening film in Berkeley. Three screenings here today and three more tomorrow.

events.title: Silkroad Art Preservation Collective: Echoes of the Silk Road
events.note: Traditional instruments from along the Silk Road performed as a touring programme rather than a museum display. The Hammer's own site reports zero events most weeks while it is actively programming, which is why South Bay theatre keeps going unreported here.

events.title: Dracula (opening night)
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Official opening of TheatreWorks' season-opening Dracula, running to 1 November. Steven Dietz's adaptation keeps Stoker's letters-and-journals structure, which is what stops the story collapsing into camp, and Giovanna Sardelli directs. The South Bay's main theatrical event of the autumn.

events.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
events.note: Second of three screenings across the weekend. Japanese programming in the small room.

events.title: Litquake: Poetry on la Veinticuatro
events.note: Litquake's Mission Spanish-language and bilingual poetry night on 24th Street, which is the right street for it. Part of the festival's opening weekend.

events.title: Smuin: French Kiss
events.note: Second of two performances this weekend; the run then goes dark until the 15th. Smuin opens its 26/27 season with a triple bill: Amy Seiwert's French Kiss, Michael Smuin's Stabat Mater revived, and a world premiere by My'Kal Stromile. The Cowell Theater is in the same Fort Mason building whose public calendar lists only the galleries, which is why a full SF dance run went unlisted here until now.

events.title: The Cook
events.note: Last evening performance before tomorrow's closing matinee.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Second of two performances today.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: Lali
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies. The festival's Saturday night slot.

events.title: Jacob Collier
events.note: Sold out. One man, a great deal of equipment, and an audience he conducts in four-part harmony whether or not it can sing. Divisive and undeniably able.

events.title: Juicebumps, Fake Fruit & Diesel Dudes
events.note: Fifteen dollars for three Bay Area post-punk bands, of which Fake Fruit are the ones to arrive for — Hannah D'Amato writes the sharpest lyrics in the local scene. The club closes at the end of the year.

events.title: Kat Robichaud's Misfit Cabaret: Final Girl
events.note: The Halloween edition of a San Francisco institution — original songs, aerialists, drag and horror-film structure, built every year from scratch. The $500 tier buys a table; the $50 one buys the same show.

events.title: Paige Fish
events.note: The Midnight Crisis tour. Confessional indie-folk with a sense of humour, in a room small enough that the between-song talking matters.

events.title: Palace with Rollo Doherty
events.note: English guitar band whose entire catalogue is one mood — reverbed, reluctant, slow — played well enough that the mood holds for ninety minutes.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Saturday evening, 8pm.

events.title: DOMi & JD BECK
events.note: Thirty-four dollars for the show that sold out Bimbo's last night. The drive over 17 is the price of admission and it is a good trade.

events.title: Electric Feels: indie rock and indie dance party
events.note: A travelling indie-sleaze club night, which in San Jose means the one place to dance to guitars after eleven. Listed for what it is.

events.title: Kafana Balkan with Inspector Gadje Balkan Brass Band
events.note: A twenty-year-old Balkan brass dance party with a live band, Jill Parker's dancers and DJ Zeljko between sets. Nobody stands still and nobody cares how you dance, which is rarer than it should be.

events.title: Ravefurrest
events.note: Hyperpop, breakcore and gabber from a furry-run rave night in the main room: live sets from Los Angeles duo Passengerprincess and the Bay Area's Sophiaaaahjkl;8901 between hardcore DJ sets. 18+, and high tempos from the first hour.

events.title: Secret Psychedelica: Libra
events.note: A psytrance collective's eighth annual Libra party: ten DJs across DNA's two smaller rooms while Ravefurrest has the main floor, running from psytrance and progressive through to psychill and breaks. Seattle's Peacedragon leads the bill. 18+.

events.title: 626 Night Market
events.note: Second of three nights. Saturday is the busiest and the queues at the better stalls are genuinely long — go at opening or go late.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T. Two performances are likely today, a matinee and an evening, but the theatre publishes neither time on its listings page. Confirm before booking.

events.title: Bart Skils
events.note: Dutch techno played at the hard, functional end. Public Works' main room is the right size and the wrong shape, which somehow helps.

events.title: Bonnie Raitt with Jon Cleary
events.note: Fifty-five years of slide guitar played with more restraint than anyone else who can do it, by a Bay Area resident in a Bay Area hall. Jon Cleary's New Orleans piano opening is not a courtesy booking. The strongest ticketed show of the weekend and the one that would be featured in a week without an air show.

events.title: Fort Mason historic district walking tour
events.note: The second-and-fourth-Saturday tour of the piers and the army's old embarkation depot. Fort Mason's calendar lists no start time or price for this, and the hill above it is a prime air-show vantage point, so expect it to be busy.

events.title: Give Until Gone: Clearcast b2b SHAKING
events.note: A local back-to-back in the loft while Bart Skils works the main room. Two rooms, one door.

events.title: High on Fire, Melvins & Windhand
events.note: The Melvins are the reason this clears the drive — forty-three years, no lineup anyone predicted, and the band every heavy act on this page descends from. High on Fire played Berkeley last night; the Melvins play nowhere else near here.

events.title: Los Horoscopos de Durango
events.note: Duranguense — the accordion-and-tuba norteno variant that briefly owned Mexican-American radio — played by the family band that defined it. One of the few Spanish-language bookings the Winery takes, and worth the hillside.

events.title: Mill Valley Film Festival 49
events.venue: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
events.note: The 49th MVFF runs 1-16 October across San Rafael, Mill Valley and Larkspur, and this weekend is its densest. Listed once rather than per screening: the festival's own site could not be read for a dated programme, so check mvff.com for today's slate. Six MVFF titles play BAMPFA in Berkeley this week if you would rather not cross the bridge.

events.title: Movements with Balance and Composure, Midrift & NIIS
events.note: Post-hardcore with the volume up and the tempos down, and Balance and Composure — reunited after six years off — underneath. A good bill in a room slightly too big for it.

events.title: Musiq Soulchild
events.note: Second night of the eight-night run, and the hardest to get into.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Night five of six. Saturday of a residency is where the covers appear.

events.title: POLO & PAN with Dabeull, Malas & STARFARI
events.note: French duo making polyglot, faintly ridiculous dance pop, with Dabeull's boogie-funk live set in support. The best-programmed club night of the week.

events.title: Taking Back Sunday, Thrice & Saves The Day
events.note: Three bands who between them defined what 2003 sounded like to a particular kind of teenager, outdoors at Stanford. Thrice have aged into the most interesting of the three. Filed as Peninsula by proximity; Stanford appears in no region list in the brief.

events.title: Tinlicker
events.note: Melodic techno in the Midway's second room while Polo & Pan run the main. Two separate tickets, one building.

events.title: tUnE-yArDs with Foxtails Brigade & Gabby La La
events.note: Merrill Garbus playing a harbour shack at the end of a dirt road past the Richmond refineries, which is the most unlikely and most appealing booking of the weekend. Richmond is in no region list in the brief; filed East Bay by proximity.

events.title: Children's Business Fair
events.note: Free to attend: children running actual stalls selling things they have made, in the County Fair Building at the Botanical Garden. Either the most wholesome market in the city or a venture-capital fever dream, depending on your disposition.

events.title: Fleet Fest
events.note: Second and final day of the ground-level festival. Ship tours continue through Monday.

events.title: All Italian Day car and motorcycle show
events.note: Fifteen dollars a head, twenty-five for a family: Alfas, Lancias, Moto Guzzis and Fiat 500s on an Alameda street, on the same day as the Italian Heritage parade across the bay. Enthusiast-run and all the better for it.

events.title: Dance Day
events.note: Free, five hours, on the Esplanade and Great Lawn: companies and community groups performing and teaching back to back. The single best free dance programme of the year in this city and almost nobody outside the neighbourhood knows it happens.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea Market
events.note: Free to browse: the second-Sunday flea run by Sunset Mercantile, vintage and makers rather than junk, on Irving between 9th and 10th. Runs April to November, so two more after this.

events.title: Model boats on parade and sailboat race
events.note: Free: the San Francisco Model Yacht Club, founded 1898, putting its fleet on the water with a race at the end. Competitive miniature sailing is exactly the sort of thing the brief means by interesting because it is strange.

events.title: Sunday Assembly Silicon Valley
events.note: A secular congregation that sings pop songs together and then listens to a talk, free, in a Masonic lodge on Castro Street. Filed under oddities with affection.

events.title: Woodside Day of the Horse: free horse fair
events.note: Second and shorter day of the free fair. Three hours, and the demonstrations are condensed.

events.title: Butchertown Jazz Festival
events.note: Free, outdoors, six hours of jazz at an urban winery in the Bayview — a neighbourhood with a jazz history nobody markets and this festival is the only thing that marks it. The T line gets you close.

events.title: Fleet Week: Travis Brass Band at the SkyStar Wheel
events.note: Free brass under the observation wheel, an hour before the air show starts.

events.title: Welcome Back Monarch Butterfly Festival
events.note: Free admission, $10 to park: the annual welcome for the overwintering monarchs in the eucalyptus grove above the beach, with guided walks into the roost. One of the last reliable monarch groves in California, which is both the appeal and the sad part, and it clears the drive on strangeness alone.

events.title: Blue Angels air show, day three
events.note: Final day, same four hours, and it overlaps the Italian Heritage parade exactly — both are in the same square mile and both are free, which makes the north waterfront impassable between noon and four. Pick one and commit, or watch the jets from the parade route.

events.title: Fleet Week: Band of the West division concert
events.note: The larger of the two Wharf concerts today, free, starting as the jets do.

events.title: Free Oakland Up market
events.note: Free: a giveaway market rather than a sale — goods redistributed at no cost. Mutual aid organised as a flea, which is a genuinely different thing from a flea.

events.title: The Whale's Tail beer garden with live music
events.note: Free to enter, drinks and food for sale, live music at the Music Concourse. The park's car-free afternoon makes this an easy drop-in.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: Eternal Trees, Eternal Mountains
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Italian Heritage Festival & Parade
events.note: Free: the oldest continuously running parade in San Francisco, from Fisherman's Wharf to Washington Square, with bands, floats and a Fleet Week ceremonial band marching in it. North Beach is unparkable today — take the 30 or the 8, or walk down from Chinatown.

events.title: Who Moves America
events.note: A Sunday-lunchtime documentary slot. Nothing about the billing was verifiable beyond the title and the time.

events.title: Jean-Luc Godard's early short films
events.note: MVFF at BAMPFA: the pre-Breathless shorts, which are rarely programmed and show him working out in public what he would spend sixty years refining.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera (matinee)
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: Sunday afternoon, and the better-value of the week's weekend performances.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: Ghost School
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: King Lear (closing matinee)
events.note: Closing performance. Z Space's Lear has run three weeks almost entirely unreported, which is a function of the venue having no central calendar rather than of the production.

events.title: MoneyHillCasino
events.note: A two o'clock all-ages matinee, which is how most of this audience can get in at all.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.note: Sunday matinee, the week's last chance at this until Tuesday.

events.title: The Cook (closing)
events.note: Final performance, with a post-show discussion. Five weeks of one of the better scripts the Rep has staged recently, closing quietly on a Sunday afternoon.

events.title: New People: NAZA
events.note: From the New People strand of contemporary Japanese cinema — a Japantown-rooted series that rarely screens anywhere else in the region. Third and last showing of the weekend.

events.title: 9 to 5 with Peaches Christ
events.note: The Dolly Parton film with a live drag pre-show from Peaches Christ, who has been doing this in that building for twenty years and remains the best reason to see a film you already own.

events.title: A Girl Unknown
events.note: MVFF's Sunday afternoon slot in Berkeley.

events.title: River of Life LGBTQ+
events.note: A queer-programming slot in the Roxie's Sunday afternoon. Descriptor is lower-confidence.

events.title: San Jose Wind Symphony: A Novel Concert
events.venue: McAfee Performing Arts and Lecture Center
events.note: A community wind band programme built around books, in a high-school auditorium with better acoustics than that implies. Students through college age get in free, and so do under-twelves with a paying adult.

events.title: 3rd i 2026: The Loyal Man
events.note: Part of 3rd i, the South Asian film festival that has run at the Roxie for over twenty years and programmes more adventurously than its budget implies.

events.title: Let's Go Bowling, Reducers SF, The Odd Numbers & Soulciter
events.note: A 4pm ska matinee: Fresno's Let's Go Bowling have been doing this since 1985, Reducers SF and The Odd Numbers are local lifers, and Soulciter spins rare grooves between sets. Four acts, daylight, and home by ten.

events.title: New People: Never After Dark
events.note: From the New People strand of contemporary Japanese cinema — a Japantown-rooted series that rarely screens anywhere else in the region. Last showing.

events.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!
events.note: Final screening of the weekend's three.

events.title: Tenor: My Name is Pati
events.note: A music documentary in the Sunday evening slot; the billing gave no more than the title.

events.title: The Dreamed Adventure
events.note: Last of the week's six MVFF screenings at BAMPFA, and the last chance to do the festival without driving to Marin.

events.title: The Phantom of the Opera
events.venue: San Jose Center for the Performing Arts
events.note: An early evening curtain, 6:30, which gets you home at a reasonable hour.

events.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Spooktacular, with Barry Bostwick
events.note: The 4K restoration with a live shadow cast from Barely Legal RHPS, a costume contest, and Barry Bostwick — the original Brad Majors — in person. Doors at six and no admittance after seven, which for this film is the difference between going and not. Resale is asking a great deal; buy from the house. The Curran is in no source list this project keeps, which is why it was missing.

events.title: Derya Yildirim & Grup Simsek with Thee Marloes
events.note: Anatolian psych played by a Hamburg-based band with a saz through a fuzz pedal, and Indonesia's Thee Marloes opening with genuinely excellent 1960s-style soul. Twenty-seven dollars for two bands you will not get another chance at.

events.title: Dhruv Sangari
events.note: Qawwali and Sufi devotional singing in the upstairs wooden hall, which is the best room in the city for an unamplified voice.

events.title: Divine Offering: celebrating the legacy of Alice Coltrane
events.note: Alice Coltrane's devotional harp-and-organ music has gone from a footnote to one of the most-borrowed sounds in contemporary music, and this is her granddaughter Sita Michelle Coltrane leading the tribute with guests. Not a repertory band playing the hits — the Ashram tapes material, which is the part that matters. The rarest thing on this week's calendar.

events.title: Edgar Alejandro
events.note: Support still unannounced at time of writing. A steep ticket for Rickshaw, which usually means a devoted audience rather than a broad one.

events.title: Santiago Cruz
events.note: Colombian singer-songwriter on the Sigo En Pie tour, partially seated — which tells you it is a listening show rather than a dance.

events.title: Don't Play With Fire
events.note: Late-night genre programming — the Roxie is the only cinema in town that still treats 8pm as early.

events.title: Ghost in the Shell: 30th Anniversary Remaster
events.note: Oshii's 1995 cyberpunk landmark in a 30th-anniversary remaster, closing the week at 8:45. The restoration is the reason to see it in a room rather than at home.

events.title: The Egyptian Lover with Love Supreme
events.note: Greg Broussard has been making Los Angeles electro on a drum machine for forty years and calls it, simply, dance music. A Sunday that works because Monday is Indigenous Peoples' Day; San Francisco's Love Supreme sound system opens. 18+.

events.title: 626 Night Market
events.note: Final night of three. Sunday closes earlier than Friday and Saturday — check before making the drive out to Pleasanton.

events.title: Air Supply
events.note: Graham Russell and Russell Hitchcock have been doing this for fifty-one years and still sing it in the original keys, which is the whole trick. A hillside at sunset is the correct setting.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest
events.note: A.C.T.'s Sunday performance; the run continues to 18 October and Oh, Mary! opens on the 13th. Curtain time unpublished per date.

events.title: Bruno Mars with Raye & DJ Pee.Wee
events.note: Second stadium night. Listed for completeness; deprioritised as the brief requires.

events.title: Chayanne
events.note: Thirty-five years of Puerto Rican pop at arena scale, with the choreography intact. Deprioritised by the brief as an arena show, but it is the biggest Spanish-language booking in the region this week.

events.title: David Byrne
events.note: A City Arts & Lectures-style evening rather than a concert — Byrne in conversation in a 900-seat former church, which is a very different proposition from the current touring show. If you want him talking rather than dancing, this is the one.

events.title: Emmet Cohen
events.note: The best young stride and bebop pianist working, who built his audience on a weekly livestream from his Harlem apartment and plays like someone who learned from the records rather than the conservatory.

events.title: Kronos Quartet
events.note: Fifty-three years of commissioning the music that did not exist yet — more than a thousand new works, most of the important American string quartet writing since 1973 — by a San Francisco institution, in the best-sounding hall on the Peninsula. The one event south of the city this week that would be the headline anywhere. Stanford is in no region list in the brief; filed Peninsula by proximity.

events.title: Litquake: A celebration of the short story
events.note: Graham Todd, Rucy Cui, Cristina Fries and William Lohier reading short fiction in a working bookbindery museum, which is the most appropriate venue Litquake has found all festival.

events.title: Musiq Soulchild
events.note: Third of eight nights. The Sunday show in a long residency is usually the loosest.

events.title: My Morning Jacket
events.note: Final night of the six-night residency. Closing nights of residencies are where the requests and the guests turn up.

events.title: Sufi Sessions San Francisco
events.note: Sufi music reframed for a club, which is either a continuation of the tradition or a departure from it depending on who you ask. The second Sufi-adjacent booking in the city tonight, which is its own kind of coincidence.

events.title: TLC with Salt-N-Pepa & En Vogue
events.note: Three acts who between them sold something like sixty million records in the 1990s, outdoors in Concord. En Vogue are the best singers on the bill and go on first. BART Concord plus the shuttle is twenty minutes and spares you the lot.
